This chunk is about:
- Places: Kolozsvár, Cluj, Hungary, Romania, Verőce
- Events: World War I, World War II, Treaty of Trianon, Second Vienna Award
- Organizations: Sixty-Four Counties Youth Movement (HVIM)
- People: László Toroczkai
- Projects: Magyar Sziget festival
- Concepts: Hungarian border revision, unification of ethnic Hungarians, Jewish ghettos

Facts:
- The Treaty of Trianon was the 1920 peace agreement that formally ended World War I between most Allied powers and the Kingdom of Hungary.
- The Treaty of Trianon reduced Hungary to a landlocked state of 93,073 square kilometers, about 28% of the 325,411 square kilometers of the pre-war Kingdom of Hungary.
- Between the Treaty of Trianon in 1920 and the Second Vienna Award in 1940, Cluj was part of Romania.
- The Kolozsvár Ghetto was one of the lesser-known Jewish ghettos of the World War II era.
- The Sixty-Four Counties Youth Movement is a far-right movement in Hungary that advocates unifying ethnic Hungarians living outside Hungary and revising the Treaty of Trianon.
- The Magyar Sziget festival is a nationalist festival in Verőce organized by the Sixty-Four Counties Youth Movement under the leadership of László Toroczkai.
